snippet:

Abstract: Intelligent agents should learn from their mistakes so that experience leads to continuous improvement. snippet:

Abstract: We present HyScale, a long-context training system for learned sparse attention. snippet:

snippet:

snippet:

Abstract: Post-training quantization (PTQ) is a key technique for efficiently deploying large language models, as it compresses weights into low-bit representations without retraining. snippet:

snippet:

Abstract: Recursive large language model (LLM) agents solve long-horizon tasks through decomposition, execution, and environmental feedback. snippet:

Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly execute tasks asynchronously: a main agent continues working while its subagents run, and the task state may change before their results arrive. title: When to Stop Penalizing Actions? Martingale GRPO for VLA Reinforcement Learning
snippet:
arXiv:2610.32431v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A failed vision-language-action (VLA) rollout does not imply that every action contributed to failure. Yet in group-relative policy optimization (GRPO), a single trajectory-level advantage is assigned to all actions in a rollout. Potentially useful recovery attempts can thus be penalized alongside the errors they aim to correct. Ideal stopping conditions for failure feedback are characterized using success-probability and policy-score martingales.
